author: DTrim99
body:
It's actually the reverse — PE allows a bit *less* than TaxAct here, and the $3,000 traces to a missing child tax credit on your TaxAct federal return.

The Alabama federal-tax deduction (Act 2022-37 worksheet) subtracts the refundable ACTC. The correct federal amounts here are 1040 line 22 tax = $13,222 and a **$3,000 fully-refundable child tax credit on line 28** (HoH, one child 6–17, AGI $104,800 — under the ARPA phase-out). PE has this: it subtracts the $3,000, giving Part I = $13,216 − $3,000 ≈ **$10,216**.

Your TaxAct federal 1040 shows line 19 (nonrefundable CTC) **and** line 28 (ACTC) both blank — no child tax credit at all — so TA's Part I had nothing to subtract and landed on $13,222. That $3,000 is TaxAct missing the CTC, not PE over-deducting.

The correct answer is actually **$10,622**, from Part II (Act 2022-37's "recompute as if under the IRC in effect 12/31/2020"): the 2020-rule CTC ($2,000) + CDCC ($600) = $2,600, so $13,222 − $2,600 = $10,622, and line 15 takes the greater of Part I ($10,222) and Part II ($10,622). Your TaxAct worksheet even printed Part II = $10,622 — it just picked the larger, incorrect Part I because its federal return omitted the CTC.

PE currently implements Part I only (no Part II / "greater-of"), so it lands ~$400 low ($10,216 vs $10,622). That's a real but small gap in our Alabama model, which we'll file. Net: PE is closer than the TaxAct figure; the $3,000 you flagged is TaxAct missing the CTC.
